public_rationale: Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing reports that subscriptions generated 20% of revenue and consumption generated 80% during January–June 2026 [e1]. This weighs against a general subscription-majority description, but does not establish the January–March 2026 mix or subscription delivery costs [e1]. OpenAI reported more than 50 million ChatGPT subscribers on March 31, 2026; that count does not establish subscription revenue share or below-cost delivery [e2]. These disclosures do not settle the required quarterly revenue and cost comparison [e1, e2].
limitations: No matched January–March 2026 revenue and delivery-cost breakdown is supplied for any of the three companies.
Anthropic's half-year GAAP breakdown cannot substitute for the target quarter's estimated mix.
The packet supplies no qualifying Cursor revenue or delivery-cost evidence.
Subscriber counts, enterprise customer classifications, financing, and company-wide losses do not establish revenue from below-cost subscriptions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most of OpenAI's, Cursor's and Anthropic's revenue comes from subsidized software subscriptions.

statement.excerpt: Even if said numbers were real, the majority of OpenAI, Cursor and Anthropic’s revenues come from subsidized software subscriptions.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is more than half of each named company's revenue, rather than more than half of their pooled revenue.
Software subscriptions include individual and enterprise subscription plans, but not separately metered API consumption merely because it is sold under a continuing contract.
Subsidized means subscription revenue fails to cover the associated cost of delivering those subscriptions. Company-wide losses or venture financing alone do not establish this.
For this ongoing observation, use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post that public evidence could report.
The surrounding argument relies on reported private-company figures, so the claimed basis is estimate rather than an explicitly stated GAAP measure.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence shows that below-delivery-cost software subscriptions generated more than 50% of realized revenue at each of OpenAI, Cursor, and Anthropic during the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that at least one named company received no more than 50% of revenue from such subscriptions during the target quarter.

evidence.explanation: The filing distinguishes enterprise commitments from subscriptions and reports consumption revenue at 80% of total revenue in the first half of 2026. This weighs against a broad subscription-majority assertion, but the half-year period and GAAP basis do not match the quarterly estimate specified in the contract.
The company discloses a large subscriber base. Subscriber counts do not establish the share of realized revenue from subscriptions or whether their delivery costs exceed their revenue.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable January–March 2026 figures for realized subscription revenue, total revenue, and attributable delivery costs. Evidence that below-cost subscriptions generated more than half of each company's revenue would support the claim; a share of half or less at any one company would contradict it.
